summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable (input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false, independently_verified=false). Thermal Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped, simulation_allowed=false), and comparison_valid=false. The reason given is that a custom experiment needs 1–128 blocks and a power_w object. The extraction supplied an empty floorplan and no power values. The scenario is Figure 6(a) of W3006943355, the transient maximum temperature for the mem2 SPEC CPU2006 set under Baseline DVFS, FLC and FBTM on a 4-core 3D-stacked NUCA cache. The extracted experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, which has no transient trace. No Ascend910 or ATPlace pinned assets or source commit were supplied, and no generated placement, input.flp or input.ptrace exists. The bundled EV6/GCC adapted demonstration was not used. There is therefore no Studio temperature to compare with the paper. The paper's reported figures are a baseline fluctuation of up to 3.5 degC, FLC/FBTM fluctuation within 0.5 degC, and about 3 degC reduction. The curves sit on a roughly 75-81 degC axis. They are not tabulated, so the observable value is null. These figures are paper-reported context only. The gate controls the final verdict, and no exact replication is claimed. At most, a qualitative statement is supportable: in the paper, lowering stacked-cache power and controlling DVFS shift peak temperature and its fluctuation, a trend that a 2D steady solve cannot test. Numerical comparison would need the same physical location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions, and these are mismatched or unknown: 3D stack versus 2D, transient versus steady, closed-loop fuzzy DVFS and cache power-gating versus fixed power, and unpublished package, heat sink, Ramb, Rv and ambient. The linked assets are only the SPEC website and a CC BY license URL, neither pinned or usable as an input.

The original system is a 3D stack with TSV-coupled cache layers above a core layer next to the heat sink. A 2D placement with no vertical layers cannot reproduce the super-core vertical heat path or the stacked cache power.

The original observable is a transient maximum-temperature time series (about 200-450 ms) from HotSpot driven by a gem5/McPAT power trace. A steady-state or one-row power trace cannot reproduce the temperature fluctuations or the control dynamics.

The original uses a closed-loop fuzzy DVFS controller with a runtime-varying thermal threshold, plus an Algorithm 1 cache-bank power-gating heuristic. The Studio runner has no equivalent controller or cache reconfiguration, so the 3 degC reduction and fluctuation claims cannot be tested.

Cooling and package details are not published: heat sink, thermal resistances Ramb and Rv, and ambient temperature. The paper also gives no HotSpot configuration (materials, layer thicknesses, grid resolution), so the solver and cooling setup cannot be matched.
The paper gives no block geometry (x, y, width, height) and no per-block power for the cores or cache zones. Any placement or power split would be illustrative and not paper-derived.
Leakage-temperature feedback in the original, Pleak depending on T per Eq. (3), is modelled in the paper's own simulations. A fixed-power thermal solve would lack this reliability-relevant coupling.
No pinned packet assets and no Studio package or material assumptions are supplied here, so none are claimed as paper-derived or matched to HotSpot.

If the runner builds a separate illustrative 2D placement and one-row power trace, its generated coordinates, powers, package and material properties are runner-made assumptions and must be kept distinct from paper facts.
Temperatures from any illustrative Studio run must not be compared numerically to the paper's Figure 6(a) curves, and no exact replication is claimed.
